(i) SN1 = Substitution, Nucleophilic, 1 = unimolecular (rate-determining step involves only one species; first order).

(ii) E is a tertiary halogenoalkane: the three bulky CH3 groups sterically hinder attack by OH− from the back (blocking SN2); the CH3 groups are electron-releasing (positive inductive effect), so the tertiary carbocation (CH3)3C+ is stable.

(iii) Step 1 (slow): the polar Cδ+–Clδ− bond breaks heterolytically (curly arrow from bond to Cl) → (CH3)3C+ + Cl−.
Step 2 (fast): OH− lone pair attacks the carbocation (curly arrow to C+) → (CH3)3COH (F, 2-methylpropan-2-ol).

A characteristic reaction (addition across C=C), e.g.:

  • CH3CH=CH2 + Br2 → CH3CHBrCH2Br (bromine water decolourised); or
  • + HBr → CH3CHBrCH3; + H2 → CH3CH2CH3; + H2O → CH3CH(OH)CH3; or
  • addition polymerisation to poly(propene), –[CH(CH3)–CH2]n–.

(i) Methyl methanoate: H–C(=O)–O–CH3 (HCOOCH3). Prepared from methanoic acid and methanol, heated with a (concentrated sulfuric) acid catalyst.

HCOOH + CH3OH ⇌ HCOOCH3 + H2O

(ii) Isomer: ethanoic acid, CH3COOH (structural formula needed, not C2H4O2).

Physical (two): boiling point of the acid is higher (hydrogen bonding between acid molecules); pH: acid < 7, ester neutral; smell: acid vinegary/pungent, ester sweet/fruity.

Chemical: the acid reacts with OH⁻ (or carbonates) to form a salt + water; the ester is hydrolysed by OH⁻ to a salt + methanol (or: the acid can be esterified, the ester cannot).

(i) 2-chloropropanoic acid: CH3–CHCl–COOH; 2-hydroxypropanoic acid: CH3–CH(OH)–COOH.

(ii) Nucleophile: an electron-pair donor (negative or neutral species with a lone pair). Required nucleophile: OH⁻ (water reacts too slowly).

(iii) Both contain a chiral carbon (C bonded to four different groups). The product is optically inactive, so the mechanism must be SN1: Cl⁻ leaves first to form a planar carbocation, which OH⁻ can attack equally from either side, giving a racemic mixture (equal amounts of both enantiomers). (SN2 would give inversion and an optically active product.)

(i) Esterification / condensation. CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O. Product: ethyl ethanoate, CH3–C(=O)–O–CH2CH3.

(ii) Catalyst: provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy (also absorbs water, shifting equilibrium right).

(iii) Acid hydrolysis: the reverse reaction occurs, giving ethanoic acid and ethanol, and the same equilibrium is set up (incomplete).

(iv) CH3COOC2H5 + OH− → CH3COO− + C2H5OH. The carboxylic acid formed reacts with the base to give the carboxylate salt, which cannot react with ethanol, so the reaction is not reversible.

The arrow must start from O, not from the H of OH−.

(iv) 1-bromopentane has the higher boiling point. 2-bromo-2-methylbutane is more branched (spherical), with less surface contact between molecules. Its London forces are therefore weaker.

(v) Esterification (condensation). Product: CH3COOCH2CH2CH2CH2CH3 (pentyl ethanoate).
